errors.problem: The letter i is both the imaginary unit and the axis index of the inner sum in one exponent. The page defined i as the axis index just before. The formula itself (negative sign, normalization 1/prod q_i) matches the paper's F_q (lines 3506-3510) tensored over the axes; only the notation clashes.

errors.quote: This bound needs power-of-two lengths, so it does not apply directly to the prime lengths $s_i$ of the integer product; the identity below supplies power-of-two transforms instead.
errors.problem: An O(q log q) operation count holds for every length q, for example through Bluestein's chirp, which the paper itself uses for the prime lengths. Only the radix-2 butterfly recursion needs powers of two. The paper's reason for power-of-two lengths is different: the synthetic transforms modulo y^r+1, with r a power of two, use powers of y as roots of unity, so multiplying by a root is a signed shift (lines 80-86). In the paper's words, 'the synthetic transforms use powers of two' (lines 3499-3500).

errors.quote: For operators $G_i$ on sequences of length $q_i$, the tensor product $\bigotimes_i G_i$ applies each $G_i$ to every line along axis $i$.
errors.problem: The tensor product is defined only for maps from length q_i to the same length q_i. The page then applies it to A_i: C^{s_i} -> C^{t_i} and B_{0,i}: C^{t_i} -> C^{s_i}, which change the line length; in the paper the array shape changes from pass to pass inside the padded box (lines 3838-3855). The mixed-product rule the page uses still holds for these rectangular maps, so the argument is unaffected.
